notes: Universal hit and block effects (drawing only: the game never reads this). One sheet in data/effects/, a row per effect, drawn as light (additive). A hit picks its row by the move's base damage: the first entry whose "below" it is under. A move with its own hitFx shows that instead. "sparks" are the newer hit effects, one strip each in data/effects/ (cut by scripts/hit-fx-prep.mjs) with its own holds, frames per drawing: a hit plays the strip named like its size (light / medium / heavy); "sparkFor" names the strip for a counter hit, a Witness counter and a projectile's hit, which come first in that order; a move whose hitFx is a strip's name ("hitFx": "slash") plays that one on a plain hit. A size with no strip falls back to its row of the old sheet (a counter one row stronger). The block flash is still the old sheet's row.

slots.notes: Effects of the universal systems (drawing only). Each sheet is in data/effects/ (cut from the owner's art in data/UniversalEffects/ with scripts/sprite-prep.mjs), one row of drawings, each held 'hold' frames; 'additive' sheets are drawn as light, the others as painted. A sheet with 'placeholder' in its file name is drawn by scripts/make-slot-placeholders.mjs and waits for real art. 'cues' = what plays once when the game reports something: 'on' is whose position (self = the fighter the cue is about, other = their opponent, between = halfway between the two, point = where the hit landed, screen = across the whole screen at the fighter's height), 'at' is feet / body / head, 'forward' moves it that many px the way the fighter faces. 'while' = what loops on a fighter for as long as they are in a state: it plays through once, then repeats from drawing 'loopFrom' (or stops on the last drawing with 'once'); 'behind' draws it behind the fighter, 'after' makes it wait that many frames, 'y' puts it that many px above the feet. 'flash' = the super flash: 'lines' is stretched over the whole screen, behind the fighters, while the game is frozen (screen effects are behind the fighters too). bodyY is in 'motion' below; headY = how far above the feet 'head' is. absorbPoseFrames = how long the vow_absorb drawing shows after an absorbed hit when the character's own art does not say (a character's vow_absorb state length wins). exTint = how strongly an EX move with no art of its own is brightened (0 to 1).

motion.notes: Movement effects (drawing only). The renderer watches each fighter's state: "enter" plays a sheet when a state starts, "leave" when it ends. "at": "feet" is the floor under the fighter, "body" is bodyY px above their feet. "trail" loops on the fighter for as long as the state lasts. "back": true draws it facing the other way (a move that travels backward). "byDrift" picks by which way the fighter was travelling: [forward, still, backward]. "alpha" thins a sheet. A fighter that jumped more than driftMax px in one frame was placed, not moving (a reset): it counts as still. Dust is drawn as painted and fades on its last drawing; "additive" sheets are drawn as light.

health.notes: The health bar's frame (drawing only; owner's art data/UI/Game_Healthbar.png, cropped to data/effects/health-frame.png). Numbers are in the frame image's pixels: window = the six corners of the empty space the bar fills (left tip, top left, top right, right tip, bottom right, bottom left). scale = size on the 960-wide screen, top = the frame's top edge from the top of the screen, gap = from the middle of the screen to the bar's inner tip, below = from the bar's lower edge down to the name. Remove this block and the plain bar is drawn as before.

devotion.notes: The Devotion meter (the super meter's look; drawing only). Pieces in data/effects/, cut from data/UniversalEffects/Game_DevotionMeter*.png. Numbers are in the frame image's pixels; the HUD draws it at 'scale', 'margin' from the screen edge and 'bottom' above the screen bottom, mirrored for Player 2. 'windows' are the bar slots [x, y, w, h], one per bar; the last one ends in a point ('tip': straight until the first x, pointed at the second). A full bar uses fillFull / glowFull. 'glowBox' places a glow around its slot, in slot widths and heights. The glow pulses between pulse.min and 1 every pulse.period frames.

layout.notes: belowFloor: nothing of the meter (its flames included) is drawn above the floor line, so it never covers feet or low attacks. lineBeside: the character mechanic's line (Moonmark...) sits beside the meter instead of above it. glowAlpha: how strong the flames are (1 = full).

impact.notes: Impact feel (drawing only, never part of the game). shake: how far the screen jolts, in px, by the hit spark size (light / medium / heavy, see "hit") and for a knockdown, wall bounce and ground bounce; it fades over "frames". 0 = no shake. flash: the fighter who is hit is drawn brighter for "frames" frames (alpha 0 to 1 = how bright; 0 = off).

shockwave.notes: Shockwave rings on big hits (drawing only, never part of the game): rings that bend the picture behind them, pushing it outward from the impact. on: false turns all of it off. charHeight: a character's height in px (ring sizes are shares of it). bands: how many steps the bend is drawn in across a ring. max: rings alive at once. edge: how bright the ring's edge is (1 = white); edgeWidth: its width as a share of the ring's thickness; fallbackEdge: the edge where the picture cannot be bent (the ring is then only light). sets: named groups of rings; scale multiplies size and strength. Per ring: delay (frames after the hit), startAt (frames of growth it already has when it appears, so it shows during hitstop), life (frames), radius (share of charHeight it grows to), thick [from, to] px, strength (px the picture is pushed at the ring's middle, fading to 0). pulse: a brief whole-screen brightening. when: which set the system's own hits play. A move plays a set when the character's art.shockwave names it: { moveOrProjectileId: setName }.

opacity.notes: How see-through every effect is drawn (drawing only), 0 to 1. An effect's own number is its "opacity" (the universal sheets in this file) or its entry in the character's art.opacity { effectOrProjectileName: number } (a mark is "mark:<var>"); one with neither takes its class below. Effects drawn as light are dimmed by it; the others become see-through. Where a sheet already has an alpha, the two multiply (air dash trail: 0.7 x 0.85 = 0.6). flashFirst: the first drawing of a hit spark. An effect whose drawn area (its cell shrunk by coverInset) covers more than coverShare of a fighter's body loses coverDrop while it does; an effect at 1 is never dropped. on: false draws everything as before. The player's Effects opacity setting multiplies all of it.

blockFx.notes: The universal block effect (owner brief, Nov 27; drawing only, every character). Two layers on one timeline, so both always show the same drawing: body = the shield (Game_Block_Effect.png, magenta keyed out), drawn flat at bodyOpacity; light = its glow (Game_Block_Effect2.png), drawn on top as light (additive). Cut by scripts/block-fx-prep.mjs on each sheet’s fixed grid, every drawing centred on the oval’s centre; lightOffset = the light’s centre minus the body’s per drawing in sheet px, as measured (corrected by the cut). sets: normal (blocked L and M normals, and projectiles under strengthOf.lightProjectileBelow base damage) and heavy (H, S and R normals, specials, supers, other projectiles); heavy has no body drawn yet (FX_BlockHeavy_Body), so it plays its light alone: add a body sprite to it when the sheet exists. in / loop / out = game frames per drawing in sheet order: drawing 4 (loop) holds for as long as the blockstun lasts (at least once), then the rest play. guard = where it sits, by the defender’s block state: [px in front of their middle, px above their feet]. charHeight x height x size = the shield’s height in game px (all layers share one scale). holdInHitstop: false = it plays through the freeze. repel: the Repel plays the normal set, size bigger, the out drawings outSpeed times faster, drifting drift px toward the attacker. on: false brings back the old block flash and Repel wave.
